nodes.label: The Making of Polyphonic Archive
nodes.blurb: The map of how Polyphonic Archive was made — the questions, tensions and craft behind turning a near-silent archive into a podcast. Four regions branch from here: what was absent, how the story was built, how it was translated between media, and the ethics beneath it all.
questions: What does it take to give voice to those the archive left silent?
When the record runs out, what may we honestly add?

nodes.label: Absence
nodes.blurb: The founding problem. The girls of Huize Dina barely speak in the surviving record. This region maps every kind of silence we worked against — and what the gaps themselves can be made to say.
questions: How can we tell the story of the girls when they are absent from the archive?
Which opportunities come with the public making of archives?

nodes.label: Absence of the girls’ voices
nodes.blurb: They were written about, but rarely heard. How do you build a story around voices the archive never kept?

nodes.label: Privacy of the individual
nodes.blurb: What the record withholds out of care — the privacy of the individual, even within an opened archive.

nodes.label: The girls’ letters
nodes.blurb: The rare moments their own words survive. Reading the letters — and deciding how to use them.

nodes.label: The implicit listener
nodes.blurb: From the implicit looker to the implicit listener — the figure the podcast is built to address.

nodes.label: Absence of records
nodes.blurb: Not only voices are missing. Whole bodies of record are gone, sealed, or were never made.

nodes.label: Censorship & the 2025 opening
nodes.blurb: The archive sat closed under a censorship period and only opened in 2025. What that timing did to the work.

nodes.label: Huize Dina’s lost archive
nodes.blurb: What the home kept of itself did not survive.

nodes.label: Lost in the war
nodes.blurb: The original Huize Dina archive was lost in the war. We work around an absence at the source.

nodes.label: Known unknowns — filling the void
nodes.blurb: Things we know of but cannot read — Mina’s letter to her grandparents among them. Where the record stops, we speculate, carefully.

nodes.label: The absence of home
nodes.blurb: Home is the missing center of these lives — as place, as mother, as belonging.

nodes.label: Is Huize Dina a home?
nodes.blurb: An institution that housed girls — but was it ever a home?

nodes.label: The absence of mothers
nodes.blurb: Mothers absent; girls becoming mothers themselves; motherhood without a husband. The Swaab and Tilly cases.

nodes.label: Storybuilding
nodes.blurb: How the material becomes a story you can be inside — dramaturgy, emphasis, sound, and the figure who carries the telling.
questions: How do you distil a narrative form from archival material?
Can the historian be the protagonist of the story?

nodes.label: An immersive story from the archive
nodes.blurb: How do you build an immersive story out of archival fragments?

nodes.label: Distilling dramatic structure
nodes.blurb: Finding dramatic and narrative structure latent in the documents.

nodes.label: Emphasis — what stays in frame
nodes.blurb: Every inclusion is an exclusion. What we used, what we left outside the frame, and why.

nodes.label: Enacting the implicit listener
nodes.blurb: Turning the implicit listener from concept into something the audience performs.

nodes.label: Virtual auditory space & binaural design
nodes.blurb: Designing a believable auditory space — binaural sound as the room the story happens in.

nodes.label: The role of music
nodes.blurb: What music does in the podcast — and where it must stay silent.

nodes.label: The historian as protagonist
nodes.blurb: Letting the researcher carry the story — the historian as the protagonist of the telling.

nodes.label: Translation between media
nodes.blurb: Everything here crosses a boundary — between space and sound, language and language, document and drama. What survives the crossing, and what changes?

nodes.label: Physical space → auditory space
nodes.blurb: Building the virtual room where the podcast happens, and the psychoacoustics that make it intuitive.

nodes.label: Between languages & times
nodes.blurb: Translating across languages and across decades — and what that asks of us.

nodes.label: Archive → podcast
nodes.blurb: What is gained and lost when a historical archive becomes a podcast?

nodes.label: Giving voice to the written text
nodes.blurb: Giving spoken voice to written text — casting, directing, and the choices that implies.

nodes.label: Ethics
nodes.blurb: The questions that sit under every other decision — truth, accuracy, AI, and the rights of people who cannot consent.

nodes.label: Art & truth
nodes.blurb: Where the documentary obligation meets the freedom of art.

nodes.label: Accuracy vs. art-making
nodes.blurb: The central tension: historical accuracy versus the making of art.

nodes.label: Is accurate representation possible?
nodes.blurb: Is an accurate representation of the past even possible — and where do we draw the line?

nodes.label: Our use of AI
nodes.blurb: AI for historically stylized translation — and the ethics of doing so.

nodes.label: Privacy & the rights of the dead
nodes.blurb: Private archival material, now public. What are the rights of the deceased? How does it touch living relatives — and can you simply contact them?
